newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex Q2 seen showing rivals' arrival.
newsitem.headline: Telmex Q2 seen showing rivals' arrival.

text.p: Second quarter results from Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) will likely show the telephone company starting to smart from the effects of long-distance competition.
Reuters interviewed four industry analysts who forecast average earnings per share during the second quarter of $0.803 per ADR -- compared with about $0.945 per ADR during the year-ago quarter.
Revenues are likely to be flat in real terms versus this year's first quarter and slightly down compared with the same quarter of last year.

"This will essentially be the fist quarter that the company will see the impact of share loss in the long-distance market, though we believe the brunt of the negative impact will be felt in the third quarter of this year," Bear Stearns analyst Rizwan Ali said in a recent report.
Telmex lost its monopoly on long-distance at the start of this year, although the market has opened in stages as different cities introduced competition at different times.
Telmex has held roughly 74 percent of the long-distance market so far.
Volumes for both domestic and international long-distance could inch higher, but revenues in both areas are seen falling as rivals cut prices to woo customers.

Some of the shortfall should be partly made up by higher tariffs for local services, where Telmex still enjoys a monopoly. But some analysts warn that Telmex already has high local rates compared with its competitors.

"The good news is their local rates, although I'm not sure how much they should depend on that. Their local rates are among the world's highest," Joanne Showalter at Caspian Securities in New York told Reuters.
The company's operating costs will rise due to a roughly 24 percent pay increase in April and higher advertising costs to fend off the competition, analysts forecast.

As a result, Arturo Vazquez of Banamex Accival brokerage in Mexico City saw Telmex's operating cash flow down six percent during the quarter, while Sari Mayer at Salomon Brothers in New York forecast (EBITDA) margins down to 57 percent compared with 62 pct in the first quarter.
Most people expect new line growth of about 100,000 during the quarter (just over one percent) as the company takes advantage of an improving economy.
Leslie Marcus at Santander Investment said a growing economy could allow volumes to soar in the third and fourth quarter of the year, offsetting competitive pressure.
